info.description:
Broker Hub — insurance brokerage platform (Phase 1: service desk + leads + client files + portal).

* All list and detail endpoints are **data-scoped on the server**: a sales rep only ever sees their
  own leads (`assigned_to`) and clients (`account_owner_id`); an id outside the caller's scope is
  answered with **404**, never 403.
* Arabic-first API messages are the client's job; codes are stable machine keys.
* Every non-2xx body is the uniform `ErrorResponse` envelope `{code, message, details}`.
* Phase 2 groups (`/policies`, `/commissions`, `/issuing-cases`, `/reports/*`) answer
  `503 feature_disabled` until the `phase2.enabled` flag is on.
info.title: Broker Hub API

post.description:
One transaction, three writes: the policy, its schedule, its commission accrual.

Gated twice, in the same order as `/commissions`: the permission first (a rep is not "blocked by a
flag", they simply do not issue policies), then the Phase-2 flag — which is what keeps a
half-configured workspace from booking policies its insurer channels cannot service yet (spec §2).

get.description: The stored file, streamed with its own filename. Scoped: a foreign policy answers 404, not 403.

The plan, with lateness applied and the commission in words (R7).

The commit is deliberate: `plan()` moves overdue rows to `late`, and a derived write that is rolled back
at the end of the request would leave the next reader disagreeing with this one.

get.description:
Authenticated *before* the stream opens, in a session that is closed before the first frame.

The dependency form (`CurrentUser` + `ScopeDep`) kept a pooled connection checked out for the entire life
of the stream — one per open tab — and starved the pool under parallel browser sessions (R7). The identity
is resolved here instead, so a stream holds a subscription and a queue, never a connection.

post.description:
Email intake (R12 §D, ADR-032): the provider-neutral signed JSON contract documented in the runbook.

Signature: `x-email-signature: sha256=<hmac(secret, raw body)>` with the `inbound_secret` credential.
With no secret configured the route refuses (403) outside dev/test — an unsigned mail firehose into
the inbox is not a default anyone should inherit.

A call to the platform's mobile number: `call.started` opens/links the request, `call.ended` closes
the timing, `recording_ready` attaches the recording we pulled and stored ourselves.
